messages:
jana (devex): FYI customer hitting failure when using Python async client + Dedicated (VPC) behind a corporate proxy on Windows. TLS handshake fails complaining about unknown CA.

jana (devex): Minimal traceback: 
```
ssl.SSLCertVerificationError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate
```

mike (py-sdk): ugh windows cert store again. Are they passing a custom CA bundle path or relying on system store?

jana (devex): they said they uploaded a PEM to the node and tried setting REDWOOD_CA_BUNDLE=/etc/ssl/certs/corp-proxy.pem but still fails. Using async client (RedwoodAsyncClient) and base_url pointed to dedicated endpoint. sync requests worked for them.

mike (py-sdk): can you paste the init snippet they used?

jana (devex): snippet they provided: 
```
from redwood import RedwoodAsyncClient
client = RedwoodAsyncClient(base_url="https://dedicated.customer.redwood.ai", proxy="http://corp-proxy:8080")
await client.chat.completions.create(...)
```

ali (infra): quick guess: aiohttp needs an SSLContext passed to the connector, env var -> process-level CA bundle might not be applied to aiohttp's connector in our wrapper. I think our async client isn't wiring ca_bundle through when base_url is non-default.

sara (eng): can confirm: I reproduced locally on Win11 + py3.11. Our AsyncClient creates ClientSession(connector=aiohttp.TCPConnector()), but we never pass ssl=ssl_context there. The sync client uses requests which honors REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE.

mike (py-sdk): ok that's a bug. short-term workaround: construct your own ssl.SSLContext and set client._session = aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=ssl_ctx)) or pass an existing session into the client if you control creation.

jana (devex): customer can't rewrite code easily — they want an argument so onboarding isn't blocked. Can we add a param like ca_bundle or ssl_context to RedwoodAsyncClient?

ali (infra): agreed. Also we should support Windows cert store: on Windows, people expect certs in the OS store to be used without manual PEM. Python's ssl.create_default_context() plus load_default_certs() should pick up system roots. We might be clobbering that when we create our own context.

sara (eng): patch idea: in async client init accept ca_bundle: Optional[str] and ssl_context: Optional[ssl.SSLContext]. If ca_bundle provided, create ctx = ssl.create_default_context(cafile=ca_bundle). Else ctx = ssl.create_default_context(); if use_windows_store_flag then ctx.load_default_certs() — and pass ctx to TCPConnector(ssl=ctx). Also add typing: ssl_context: Optional[ssl.SSLContext] in signature.

mike (py-sdk): sounds good. tiny api note: prefer param name trust_bundle or cafile to match certifi/requests naming. Also add env var override REDWOOD_SSL_CA or REDWOOD_SSL_CONTEXT for automation.

jana (devex): customer tested manual hack and confirmed it fixes it: 
```
import ssl
import aiohttp
from redwood import RedwoodAsyncClient
ctx = ssl.create_default_context()
ctx.load_verify_locations(r"C:\\internal_certs\\corp-proxy.pem")
session = aiohttp.ClientSession(connector=aiohttp.TCPConnector(ssl=ctx))
client = RedwoodAsyncClient(base_url="https://dedicated.customer.redwood.ai", session=session)
await client.chat.completions.create(...)
```

ali (infra): thanks for repro. I'll open a GH issue/PR template for adding cafile/ssl_context support + tests on Windows. We should also add a unit/integration test that simulates a proxy CA.

mike (py-sdk): please include typing change request in issue: mypy-friendly type for ssl_context, and document behavior of env vars vs param precedence. Also doc sample for Windows: use load_verify_locations + path quoting.

ci-bot: Created issue redwood/redwood-py#482: "async client: support cafile / ssl_context + windows cert store handling" by ali.

jana (devex): linking to customer ticket so support can coordinate: TICKET-1142. Thanks everyone — keeping customer updated. :thumbsup:
